slides.heading: Protein Denaturation: Egg White Sets
bullets: How heating sets egg white: folded protein chains unfold in gentle heat, bond into a network that traps the water, and the white turns opaque and firm
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one egg white through the whole denaturation change, from clear and runny to opaque and firmly set.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Describe protein denaturation in order: folded chains, unfolding, bonding into a network, set white
Explain why the set white still holds its water inside the protein network
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to order every stage of the change and explain where the water is when the white has set.

slides.heading: A runny white turns firm - where did the water go?
bullets: The white starts clear and runny, spreading loosely in the pan
So what actually makes it turn opaque and hold its shape?
slides.notes: Ask the class: the cooked white looks drier than the raw white, so has the water left it? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the water never leaves - it is trapped.

slides.heading: The water stays - the chains unfold and net together
bullets: Gentle heat unfolds the tightly folded protein chains in the white
The unfolded chains bond to each other and build a network
The network traps the water in its pockets, so the white turns opaque and sets firm
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: setting is a change in the protein chains, not a loss of water - the chains unfold, bond, and hold the water inside the network they form.

slides.heading: Raw: folded chains in clear runny white
bullets: Raw egg white is clear and runny, spreading loosely in the pan
Inside it, each protein chain is folded into a tight coil
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the folded chains in the clear white: name the starting state before any heat is applied.

slides.heading: Gentle heat: the folded chains unfold
bullets: The pan warms gently from below
The heat gives the folded chains energy to open out, and each tight coil unfolds into a long loose chain
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and watch the coils open out: the chains are unfolded now, but the white has not set yet.

slides.heading: Bonding: chains net together, trap water
bullets: The unfolded chains link to each other with new bonds
The bonds build a network, and the water is trapped in the pockets of the network as the white turns opaque
slides.notes: Play scene 3 slowly: watch the chains bond into a net - the water stays where it is, held in the pockets of the network.

slides.heading: Set: firm white, water still trapped
bullets: The white is fully set: opaque, firm, and holding its shape
Lifted out of the pan it does not run, and the water is still trapped inside its network
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and follow the set white out of the pan: it holds its shape because the bonded network holds both itself and its water.

slides.heading: Worked example: tracing one white as it cooks
bullets: Start with folded chains in clear runny white, warm the pan gently so the chains unfold, and let the unfolded chains bond into a network
The network traps the water, the white turns opaque, and it sets firm with its water still inside
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, folded chains in runny white. Step 2, gentle heat unfolds the chains. Step 3, the chains bond and net the water in. Step 4, the white is set firm, water still trapped.

slides.heading: Your turn: order the change
bullets: In pairs: put folded, unfolding, bonding and set in order, and say where the water is at the final stage
Then swap and check: did your partner say the water stays trapped in the network, instead of leaving the white?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for trapped-water reasoning, then take two pairs answers: heat unfolds the chains, the chains bond into a network, and the water stays trapped inside it.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says the white sets because its water leaves as it cooks
Name what unfolds, what bonds, and where the water ends up to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers follow the chains - unfold, bond, network - and keep the water inside the network.
